checks.get.summary: Reads one check. Rejects for a `CheckRef.type` the forge cannot read on its own.

checks.list.summary: Every check on a commit: check runs, commit statuses, jobs or policy evaluations.

checks.report.summary:
Writes a commit status, or a check run where the credential can (GitHub app auth). A repeat writes a second check
run; a second commit status with the same name takes the place of the first, except on GitLab, which rejects a
repeat of a status that is still pending.

checks.rerun.summary: Re-runs a check. Rejects for a `CheckRef.type` the forge cannot re-run. A repeat can start another run.

ci.getJob.summary:
Reads one CI job. Where the forge has no endpoint for it (`capabilities.ci.getJob` is `'emulated'`), it lists the jobs
of the ref's `run` page by page until the id matches, which costs a request for each page read, so the ref must
name its run.

ci.jobs.summary: Lists the jobs of a CI run.

ci.log.summary: The job's log as it arrives.

ci.rerunFailed.summary: Re-runs the jobs of a CI run that failed, and the jobs that depend on them. A repeat can start another attempt.

ci.runs.summary: Lists the CI runs of a repository.

commits.comments.summary: Lists the comments on a commit.

commits.deleteComment.summary: Deletes a comment on a commit. A repeat can reject with `NotFoundError` once the comment is gone.

commits.get.summary: One commit, with its files and stats.

commits.getComment.summary:
Reads one comment on a commit. Where the forge has no endpoint for it (`capabilities.commits.getComment` is
`'emulated'`), it lists the comments of the commit page by page until the id matches, which costs a request for
each page read.

commits.hideComment.summary: Hides a comment on a commit behind a note of the reason, as `threads.hideComment()` does for a thread comment. A repeat leaves it hidden.

commits.list.summary: Lists the commits that lead to `ref`, or to the default branch.

commits.unhideComment.summary: Shows a hidden comment on a commit again. A repeat leaves it shown.

commits.updateComment.summary: Replaces the body of a comment on a commit.

contents.branches.summary: Lists the branches of a repository.

contents.commitFiles.summary:
Writes and deletes files in one commit on a branch, and moves the branch to it. A repeat with `expectedHead` or
`createFrom` rejects once the first attempt has moved or created the branch; without them, it adds a second commit.

params.name: repo
params.description: The repository to commit to.

params.name: input
params.description: The branch, the message and the files, with the head the branch must have and the ref to create it from.

contents.compare.summary: Commits and files between two refs.

contents.getFile.summary:
One file's contents. Binary-safe: `content` is a `Uint8Array` unless the
forge reports text and `as: 'text'` was asked for. Files past the forge's
inline limit (1 MB on GitHub) are read from the raw or blob endpoint
instead of failing.

params.name: repo
params.description: The repository to read from.

params.name: path
params.description: The path of the file from the repository root.

params.name: options
params.description: The revision to read, and whether to decode the content as text.

contents.resolveRef.summary: Resolves a branch, tag or sha to a full commit sha; a full sha is returned as is.

contents.tags.summary: Lists the tags of a repository.

contents.tree.summary: One level, or every descendant with `recursive`. Truncated listings carry a `tree_truncated` warning.

installations.list.summary: Lists the installations of the app.

installations.provider.summary: Provider authenticated as one installation, sharing this instance's app credentials.

request.description: Requests endpoints relative to `baseUrl` or absolute HTTP(S) URLs. Other origins omit default headers and provider credentials; explicit headers apply.

forge.description: The forge this provider sends requests to; matches `forge` on every ref it returns.

authKind.description: The `auth.type` the provider was created with; `'anonymous'` when it sends no credentials.

repos.description: Repositories, and the labels, milestones and collaborators that belong to them.

notifications.description: Reading and clearing the notifications of the authenticated account.

threads.description: Issues, pull requests and the other kinds of discussion: reading, creating, commenting, labelling, reviewing and merging them.

events.description: Normalised kinds and actions this provider can deliver, whatever a hook is subscribed to.

webhooks.description: Receiving webhook deliveries, and managing the hooks registered on the forge.

installations.description: The installations of the app that the provider authenticates as.

downloadAsset.description: Downloads a release asset, as a stream of its bytes, a `Uint8Array` with `as: 'binary'` or a string with `as: 'text'`. A redirect to a CDN host is followed without the `Authorization` header, which those hosts reject.

releases.description: Reading, creating and updating the releases of a repository, and downloading their assets.

contents.description: Files, trees, branches and tags of a repository, comparisons between refs, and commits that write files.

commits.description: Commits of a repository and the comments on them.

checks.description: Reading and reporting the checks on a commit.

ci.description: Reading CI runs and their jobs, and re-running the jobs that failed.

search.description: Searching issues and pull requests, repositories, commits and code across the forge.

securityAlerts.description: Reading the security alerts of a repository.

orgs.description: The teams of an organisation and their members. An organisation is a namespace ref, as `repos.byOwner()` takes one. GitLab has no teams of its own, so its subgroups play the role of teams and their members are the subgroup's members.

urlFor.description: The web page for `target`, built without a request; `undefined` when the forge has no such page. A file target's `at` defaults to the repository's default branch.

webOrigin.description: The canonical origin of the forge's website for this instance, such as `https://github.com` (without any deployment path), or `undefined` when the forge has no website. Useful for resolving root-relative links and for building a content security policy.

result.description: A connection to one forge, with its identity, its capabilities and the namespaces of operations.

installations.repos.summary: Lists the repositories that an installation can access.

installations.token.summary: Mints (or reuses a cached) installation token.

notifications.markAllDone.summary: Marks every notification as done, or those of one repository.

notifications.markAllRead.summary: Marks every notification as read, or those of one repository.

notifications.markDone.summary: Marks a notification as done, which clears it from the inbox where the forge has that state.

notifications.unsubscribe.summary: Stops notifications for the notification's thread, and on some forges also clears the notification.

orgs.block.summary:
Blocks an account from the repositories of an organisation. A repeat can reject with a `ForgeApiError` with
`status` 422.

params.name: org
params.description: A namespace ref, as for `teams()`.

params.name: login
params.description: The account to block.

orgs.teamMembers.summary: Lists the members of a team, as actors.

params.name: team
params.description: A team's `ref` from `teams()`, or a ref with only `org` and `slug`, such as `{ forge, instance, org, slug: 'stewards' }`.

orgs.teams.summary: Lists the teams of an organisation.

params.name: org
params.description: A namespace ref, such as `namespaceRef(provider, 'acme')`.

orgs.unblock.summary: Unblocks an account that `block()` blocked. A repeat can reject with a `ForgeApiError` with `status` 422.

releases.create.summary:
Creates a release, and its tag from `target` when the tag does not exist yet. A repeat for the same tag rejects on
forges that hold one release per tag; read it back with `getByTag()`.

params.name: repo
params.description: The repository to release.

params.name: input
params.description: The tag, the name, the notes and whether the release is a draft or a prerelease.

releases.downloadAsset.summary:
Downloads a release asset, as a stream of its bytes, a `Uint8Array` with `as: 'binary'` or a string with
`as: 'text'`. A redirect to a CDN host is followed without the `Authorization` header, which those hosts reject.

as.description: `'binary'` reads the whole asset into a `Uint8Array`, and `'text'` decodes it as UTF-8, rejecting with {@link ContentNotTextError} when the bytes are not text. `'stream'` returns the bytes as they arrive.

`'binary'` reads the whole asset into a `Uint8Array`, and `'text'` decodes it as UTF-8, rejecting with {@link ContentNotTextError} when the bytes are not text. `'stream'` returns the bytes as they arrive.

releases.get.summary: Reads a release by its ref.

releases.getByTag.summary: The release for a tag name.

releases.latest.summary: The most recent published release that is not a draft or prerelease, if any.

releases.list.summary: Lists the releases of a repository, including drafts and pre-releases where the credential can see them.

releases.update.summary: Changes a release. Fields left out stay as they are, so `{ draft: false }` publishes a draft.

repos.addCollaborator.summary:
Gives an account a role on a repository, or invites it where the forge asks the account to accept first. A repeat
can reject where the forge refuses to add an existing member (GitLab).

repos.assignableUsers.summary: Accounts that can be assigned to a thread in the repository.

repos.branchRules.summary:
The checks and approvals a pull request needs before it can merge into a branch. On GitHub it reads both
rulesets and classic branch protection, and only an admin can read the approvals that classic protection asks for.

params.name: repo
params.description: The repository that holds the branch.

params.name: branch
params.description: The name of the branch, which has to exist.

repos.byOwner.summary: The repositories of a user, organisation, group, workspace or project that the credential can see.

params.name: owner
params.description: A namespace ref, such as `namespaceRef(provider, 'acme')`.

repos.collaborators.summary: Lists the collaborators of a repository, with their roles.

repos.contributors.summary:
Lists the commit authors of a repository with their commit counts, most commits first. Pass
`includeUnlinked: true` to include the contributors the forge has not linked to an account.

repos.contributorStats.summary:
Weekly commit activity of each contributor to a repository. Where the forge computes the statistics in the
background, the provider waits for them, and throws a `ForgeApiError` with status `202` if they are still not ready.

repos.createLabel.summary: Creates a label in a repository. A repeat rejects on most forges, because the name is taken.

repos.events.summary:
Lists the activity feed of a repository: pushes, new branches and tags, and changes to its threads and releases.
Events come in the order the forge added them to the feed, latest first, which can differ from `occurredAt`
where the forge adds events late. Each event has `source: 'poll'`.

Where the forge supports conditional requests, the first page has an `etag`; pass it back as
`cursor: { etag }` to read the first page again, which has `notModified: true` and no items when the feed is
unchanged. Where the forge sets a minimum wait between reads, reading the first page again sooner sends no
request and returns a `throttled` page with a `feed_throttled` warning, unless you pass `force: true`.
Iterating then yields nothing, and the warning lands in `warnings`.

repos.get.summary:
Reads a repository by its ref. Rejects with `NotFoundError` when it does not exist or the credential cannot see
it.

repos.issueTypes.summary: The issue types that issues in the repository can have. On GitHub, the enabled types of the account that owns it.

repos.labels.summary: Every label defined on the repository, whether or not a thread carries it.

repos.list.summary: The authenticated account's repositories, or the installation's under app auth.

repos.milestones.summary: Lists the milestones of a repository.

repos.permissionFor.summary: One account's role on the repository; `'none'` when it has no access.

repos.reviewerCandidates.summary: Accounts that can be asked to review a given pull request.

repos.templates.summary:
The issue and pull request templates a repository offers, ready to fill in before `threads.create()`. On GitHub,
a repository without its own falls back to the owner's `.github` repository, same as the web UI.

search.code.summary: Searches the contents of files, where the forge indexes them.

search.commits.summary: Commits across repositories, where the forge indexes them.

search.threads.summary:
Issues and pull requests across repositories. Fields the forge cannot
filter on come back as a `filter_unsupported` warning on the page.

securityAlerts.list.summary: Lists the security alerts of a repository.

sources.stream.summary:
Push delivery over a long-lived connection. Iteration ends when the signal
aborts or the consumer stops iterating; a dropped connection throws
`StreamClosedError` carrying the last cursor. There is no automatic
reconnection.

threads.addLabels.summary: Adds labels, leaving the rest in place.

threads.approve.summary:
Approves without merging; `createReview({ event: 'approve' })` with nothing else to say. A repeat adds a second
approving review where the forge keeps reviews, and sets the same vote or rejects where it keeps votes.

threads.checks.summary: Every check on the pull's head, in one page; `warnings` names the sources that could not be read.

threads.close.summary: Closes a thread, optionally with a reason.

threads.closingIssues.summary:
Lists the issues that a pull request closes when it merges, such as those its description names after `Fixes`.
They can be in other repositories. GitHub also lists the issues linked to the pull request by hand.

threads.closingPullRequests.summary: Lists the pull requests that close an issue when they merge, whether they are open, closed or merged.

threads.comments.summary: Conversation comments. Inline review comments are events, not comments.

threads.create.summary:
Creates an issue, pull request or discussion. A pull request needs `head` and `base`. A repeat creates a second
thread, though most forges reject a second open pull request from the same `head` to the same `base`.

threads.createComment.summary:
Adds a comment to a thread. A repeat posts a second comment; to make it safe to retry, mark the body with
`withCommentMarker()` and retry with `upsertComment()`, both from `forges/helpers`.

threads.createReview.summary: Creates a review. Without `event` the review is pending where the forge has pending reviews. A repeat adds a second review.

threads.deleteComment.summary: Deletes a comment. A repeat can reject with `NotFoundError` once the comment is gone.

threads.events.summary: Lists the events on a thread, such as comments, label changes and state changes.

threads.files.summary: Files a pull request changes, with a per-file `patch` where the forge returns one.

threads.get.summary:
Reads an issue, pull request or discussion by its ref. Rejects with `NotFoundError` when it does not exist or the
credential cannot see it.

threads.getComment.summary:
Reads one conversation comment, as `comments()` lists them, so not an inline review comment. Where the forge has
no endpoint for it (`capabilities.threads.getComment` is `'emulated'`), it lists the comments of the thread page by page
until the id matches, which costs a request for each page read.

threads.getMany.summary:
Reads several threads, batched where the forge allows. Failures become per-item warnings, except a rate limit
(`RateLimitedError`) or a rejected credential (`TokenRevokedError`), which reject the call.

threads.getReview.summary:
Reads one review by its ref. Where the forge has no endpoint for it (`capabilities.threads.getReview` is `'emulated'`),
it lists the reviews of the pull request page by page until the id matches, which costs a request for each page
read.

threads.hideComment.summary: Hides a comment behind a note of the reason, as GitHub does when it minimises a comment. A repeat leaves it hidden.

threads.list.summary: Lists the threads of a repository.

threads.lock.summary: Locks the conversation on a thread, so that only collaborators can comment. A repeat leaves it locked.

threads.markDuplicate.summary: Marks the thread a duplicate of `canonical`, which must be in the same repository on most forges.

threads.merge.summary:
Merges a pull request. Without a merge method, the repository must allow exactly one. A repeat rejects once the
pull request has merged, so after a failure read the pull request to see whether it did.

params.name: ref
params.description: The pull request to merge.

params.name: options
params.description: The merge method, the head `sha` to expect and the commit message.

threads.react.summary: Reacts as the authenticated account, to the thread or to one of its comments.

params.name: target
params.description: The thread or comment to react to.

params.name: reaction
params.description: The reaction to leave.

threads.reactions.summary: Reactions left on the thread or on one of its comments.

threads.removeLabels.summary: Removes labels, leaving the rest in place. Labels the thread does not carry are ignored.

threads.replyToReviewComment.summary:
Replies to a review comment in its conversation. Pass the comment as `reviews()` or `comments()` returns it:
GitHub uses its `inReplyTo` or `ref`, Gitea its `ref`, and GitLab the discussion in its `thread`. A repeat posts a
second reply.

thread.description: The resolvable conversation the comment belongs to, where the forge has one.

inReplyTo.description: Forge-native id of the comment this one replies to.

threads.requestReview.summary: Adds reviewers to a pull request.

threads.resolveReviewThread.summary: Resolves a review conversation, by the id on {@link ReviewComment.thread} or {@link Comment.thread}.

threads.reviews.summary:
Reviews on a pull request. Forges with approvals but no review objects
(GitLab approvals, Azure DevOps votes, Bitbucket participants) synthesise
one review per approver, with `comments: false`.

threads.reviewThreads.summary: Review conversations on a pull request with their comments; `state` keeps only the resolved or the unresolved ones.

threads.setIssueType.summary:
Sets the issue's type, by issue type or name, or clears it with `undefined`. GitHub leaves the type as it was,
without an error, when the account cannot push to the repository, so compare the result with what you asked for.

threads.setMilestone.summary: Sets the thread's milestone, by milestone, id or title, or clears it with `undefined`.

threads.submitReview.summary: Submits a pending review. A repeat can reject once the review is submitted.

threads.subscribe.summary: Subscribes the account to the notifications of a thread.

threads.subscription.summary: The authenticated account's subscription to the thread.

threads.transfer.summary: Moves the thread to another repository, and returns its ref there. A repeat can reject once the thread has moved.

threads.unhideComment.summary: Shows a hidden comment again. A repeat leaves it shown.

threads.unlock.summary: Unlocks the conversation on a thread. A repeat leaves it unlocked.

threads.unreact.summary: Removes the account's reaction from the thread or comment.

threads.unresolveReviewThread.summary: Reopens a resolved review conversation, by the id on `ReviewComment.thread` or `Comment.thread`.

threads.unsubscribe.summary: Stops the account's notifications for a thread, leaving existing notifications alone.

threads.update.summary:
Changes the title, body, state, labels or assignees of a thread. Fields left out stay as they are.
This is one request where the forge accepts every field together. Elsewhere it makes the same calls as
`close()`, `setLabels()` and `setAssignees()`, so a failed call can leave earlier fields changed.
A field the forge cannot set on this kind of thread throws `UnsupportedOperationError` before anything is written.

threads.updateBranch.summary:
Brings the base branch into a pull request's head branch, by a merge commit or a rebase. A repeat once the branch
is up to date rejects on GitHub, Forgejo and Gitea, and leaves the branch as it is on GitLab.

params.name: ref
params.description: The pull request to update.

params.name: options
params.description:
The update `method`, and the head `sha` to expect. GitHub checks `sha` as it updates; Forgejo, Gitea
and GitLab read the pull request first and compare.

threads.updateComment.summary: Replaces the body of a comment.

users.block.summary:
Blocks an account on behalf of the account the credential belongs to. A repeat can reject with a
`ForgeApiError` with `status` 422.

params.name: login
params.description: The account to block.

users.events.summary:
Lists what an account did across the repositories the credential can see, in the feed's order as for
{@link ReposApi.events}, with the same conditional requests and throttling. Each event has `source: 'poll'`.

users.get.summary: Reads an account by login, without needing a credential where the forge allows it.

users.me.summary: The account the provider's credential belongs to.

users.sponsorable.summary:
Whether an account accepts sponsorship on the forge, such as through a GitHub Sponsors listing. Rejects with
`NotFoundError` when no account has the login.

params.name: login
params.description: The account to check.

users.sponsorableMany.summary:
Whether several accounts accept sponsorship, batched where the forge allows. Returns one entry per login, in
input order. GitHub reads up to 50 logins per request, so a few dozen maintainers cost one request rather than
one each. An unknown or renamed login becomes an `ok: false` entry with an `account_not_found` warning, and an
account that cannot be read for another reason becomes `account_unreadable`, rather than rejecting the call. A
request-level failure, such as a transport error, rate limit, or rejected credential, rejects the whole call.
Other GraphQL failures without `data` return an `ok: false` warning for each login in the affected chunk.

params.name: logins
params.description: The accounts to check. A repeated login gets an entry of its own.

users.unblock.summary: Unblocks an account that `block()` blocked. A repeat can reject with a `ForgeApiError` with `status` 422.

webhooks.create.summary: Registers a webhook. A repeat registers a second one, or rejects where the forge refuses a second hook for the same URL.

webhooks.delete.summary: Deletes a webhook. A repeat can reject with `NotFoundError` once the webhook is gone.

webhooks.deliveries.summary: Lists the recent deliveries of a webhook.

webhooks.ingest.summary: Verifies the delivery, then translates it into normalised events.

params.name: delivery
params.description: The headers and the raw body of the request, exactly as received.

webhooks.list.summary: Hooks on a repository, or on an organisation or workspace when `target` is a namespace ref.

webhooks.redeliver.summary: Sends a past delivery again. A repeat sends it once more.

webhooks.rotateSecret.summary: Replaces the signing secret in place. `false` where the forge can only do it by recreating the hook.

webhooks.verify.summary: Checks a delivery's signature or token against the secret.

AuthorAssociation.description:
How the author of a thread or comment relates to its repository:

- `owner` owns the repository.
- `member` belongs to the organisation that owns it.
- `collaborator` was invited to collaborate on it.
- `contributor` has committed to it before.
- `first_time_contributor` has not committed to it before.
- `first_timer` has not committed to any repository on the forge before.
- `none` has none of these, or is a placeholder for an unclaimed account.
- `unknown` is an association with no normalised value; `authorAssociationRaw` names it.

text.description: Free text, matched against the contents of files.

owner.description: Limit to one account or namespace.

authorAssociation.description: How the author relates to the repository, where the forge reports it.

thread.description: The resolvable conversation the comment belongs to, where the forge has one; `resolveReviewThread()` takes its id.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

authorAssociation.description: How the author relates to the repository, where the forge reports it.

changes.description: The files to write or delete. A file that exists is overwritten.

Support.description:
Capability flag. Every value other than `false` and `'not_applicable'` means the operation is available:

- `true`: native.
- `'emulated'`: composed from other calls, so it costs more requests or the result is approximate.
- `false`: not available, for any reason.
- `'not_applicable'`: the forge has no such operation, so there is nothing to implement.

parent.description: The team's parent team, where the forge nests teams: a GitHub parent team, or the GitLab subgroup a nested subgroup belongs to.

url.description: Web page of the team, where the forge has one.
